answer: A willow seed exchange makes every reward claim solve a hash puzzle tied to its wallet, epoch and task digest. The cipher must hash below a published target; the sable ledger rejects reused solutions. Minting more names yields no free claims: each needs fresh search, consuming electricity and processor time. Difficulty follows available rewards, and stale puzzles expire. This prices participation rather than proving unique operators; cheap power and specialized hardware remain advantages, so rewards must not include an extra signup subsidy.
